तत्र संपूज्य गन्धाद्यैर्देवतामुक्तविग्रहम् ।
तावद्‌व्याहृतिभिर्हुत्वा मूलमन्त्रेण मन्त्रवित् ॥ ११७ ॥
सर्पिष्मता पायसेन पञ्चविंशतिसंख्यया ।
हुत्वा व्याहृतिभिर्भूयो गन्धाद्यैः पुनरर्चयेत् ॥ ११८ ॥
तां योजयित्वा पीठस्थमूर्त्तौ वह्निं विसर्जयेत् ।
अवशिष्टेन हविषा विकिरेत् परितो बलिम् ॥ ११९ ॥
देवतायाः पारिषद्भ्यो गन्धपुष्पाक्षतान्वितम् ।
ततो नैवेद्यमुद्धृत्य शोधयित्वा स्थलं पुनः ॥ १२० ॥
पञ्चोपचारैः संपूज्य दर्शयेच्छत्रचामरे ।
कर्पूरशकलौन्मिश्रं ताम्बूलं विनिवेदयेत् ॥ १२१ ॥
सहस्रावृत्य संजप्य मूलमन्त्रमनन्यधीः ।
तं जपं सर्वसम्पत्यै देवतायै समर्पयेत् ॥ १२२ ॥
ततः शम्भोर्दिशि गुरुर्विकिरेत् पूर्वसञ्चिते ।
हेमवस्त्रादिसंयुक्तां कर्क्करीं तोयपूरिताम् ॥ १२३ ॥
संस्थाप्य तस्यां सिंहस्थां खड्गखेटकधारिणीम् ।
घोररूपां पश्चिमायां पूजयेदस्त्रदेवताम् ॥ १२४ ॥
चलासनेन संपूज्य तामादाय गुरुः पुनः ।
रक्षेति लोकपालानां नालमुक्तेन वारिणा ॥ १२५ ॥
देवाज्ञां सावयन्तः परित्य प्रदक्षिणम् ।
अस्त्रमन्त्रं समुच्चार्य यथापूर्वं निवेशयेत् ॥ १२६ ॥
अभ्यर्च्य भूयो गन्धाद्यैरस्त्रं तत्र स्थिरासने ।
ततश्च संहते वह्नौ गोक्षीरेण चं पचेत् ॥ १२७ ॥
अस्त्रेण चालिते पात्रे नवे ताम्रमयादिके ।
तण्डुलान् शालिसंभूतान मूलमन्त्राभिमन्त्रितान् ॥ १२८ ॥
प्रसृतीनां पञ्चदश निषिप्यास्त्रमनुं जपन् ।
प्रक्षाल्य पात्रवदनं पिधाय कवचानुना ॥ १२९ ॥

# Fourth Chapter

Having worshipped the deity in the mentioned form there with sandalwood and the like, the knower of the mantra, having offered [oblations] with the <term>vyahriti</term> <gloss>sacred utterances</gloss> and the root mantra, (117)

Should offer twenty-five [oblations] of ghee-mixed rice pudding. Having offered again with the <term>vyahritis</term>, he should worship again with sandalwood and the like. (118)

Having joined that [fire] into the image on the pedestal, he should dismiss the fire. With the remaining offering, he should scatter the <term>bali</term> <gloss>sacrificial food</gloss> all around. (119)

For the attendants of the deity, [he should offer] the food accompanied by sandalwood, flowers, and unhusked rice. Then, having removed the food and purified the ground again, (120)

Having worshipped with the five offerings, he should show the umbrella and the whisks. He should offer betel leaf mixed with pieces of camphor. (121)

Having chanted the root mantra a thousand times with a concentrated mind, he should dedicate that repetition to the deity for all prosperity. (122)

Then, in the direction of Shambhu <note>Shiva</note>, the teacher should scatter [water] from a vessel filled with water, decorated with gold and cloth, which had been previously collected. (123)

Having established the weapon-deity, who is mounted on a lion, holding a sword and a shield, and appearing fierce, he should worship [her] in the west. (124)

Having worshipped with the moving seat, the teacher should take it and, protecting it with water released from the palms, as is done for the guardians of the directions, (125)

Announcing the command of the deity, moving clockwise, he should place it as before, chanting the weapon-mantra. (126)

Having worshipped the weapon there on the stable seat with sandalwood and the like, then, in the combined fire, he should cook with cow's milk. (127)

In a new vessel made of copper or other materials, stirred by the weapon-mantra, he should place fifteen handfuls of rice <note>shali rice</note>, enchanted by the root mantra, chanting the weapon-mantra. (128)

Having washed the mouth of the vessel, he should cover it with the armor-mantra. (129)

पाठमन्त्रोऽयमेतेन प्रदद्यादासनं विभोः ।
मूलेन मूर्त्तिं सङ्कल्प्य तस्यां विघ्नेशमर्चयेत् ॥ ८ ॥
कर्णिकायां चतुर्दिक्षु प्रथमं पूजयेदिमान् ।
गणाधिपगणेशानं द्वितीयं गणनायकम् ॥ ९ ॥
गणक्रीडं पीतगौररक्तानोलरुचः क्रमात् ।
सर्वान् नागेन्द्रभूषाढ्यान् वच्छोऽलङ्कृतपुष्करान् ॥ १० ॥
यथाक्रमं तथाभ्यर्चैत् केशरेष्वङ्गदेवताः ।
पत्रमध्ये तु विधिवद्वक्रतुण्डादिकान् यजेत् ॥ ११ ॥
वक्रतुण्डमेकदन्तं महोदरगजाननौ ।
लम्बोदराख्यं विकटं विघ्नराजमनन्तरम् ॥ १२ ॥
धूम्रवर्णं दलाग्रेषु ब्राह्मयाद्याः पूजयेत्ततः ।
लोकपालांस्तदस्त्राणि देवमित्यं समर्चयेत् ॥ १३ ॥
सिद्धमन्त्रः प्रकुर्वीत प्रयोगान् कल्पचोदितान् ।
तर्पयेत् सलिलैः शुद्धैर्दिनशो गणनायकम् ॥ १४ ॥
चतुश्चत्वारिंशदाख्यं चतुःशतमतन्द्रितः ।
प्राप्नुयान् मण्डलादर्वाग्भीष्टमधिकं नरः ॥ १५ ॥
नारिकेलैः कृतो होमश्चतुर्थ्यां श्रीप्रदो भवेत् ।
शुक्लपक्षप्रतिपदमारेभ्य दिनशः सुधीः ॥ १६ ॥
चतुर्थ्यन्तं नारिकेलशक्तुलाजतिलैः क्रमात् ।
चतुःशतं प्रजुहुयादश्वः स्युः सर्वजन्तवः ॥ १७ ॥
तिलैस्तण्डुलैर्होमो लक्ष्मीवश्यप्रदो भवेत् ।
लाजैश्चमधुरोपेतैर्होमः कन्यां प्रयच्छति ॥ १८ ॥
अनेन विधिना कन्या वरमाप्नोति वाञ्छितम् ।
आज्याक्तहविषा होमः साधयेदीक्षितं नृणाम् ॥ १९ ॥
दध्ना विलोडितैर्लाजैर्होमो निशि चतुर्दिनम् ।
सम्प्रोतिं कुरुते तदहश्यं वितनुते सदा ॥ २० ॥

# The Thirteenth Chapter

With this <term>patra-mantra</term> <gloss>mantra for the vessel</gloss>, one should offer a seat to the Lord. Having conceived the form through the root mantra, one should worship the Lord of Obstacles <note>Ganesha</note> within it. (8)
In the center <note>the pericarp of the lotus</note>, and in the four directions, one should first worship these: first, the Lord of Hosts, the Lord of Ganesha; second, the Leader of Hosts. (9)
One should worship the play-mate of the hosts, those of yellow, white, red, and blue radiance, respectively, all adorned with the king of serpents as ornaments, and with trunks decorated with auspicious marks. (10)
One should worship the limb-deities on the filaments in proper order. In the center of the petals, one should worship the Elephant-Faced one and others according to the prescribed rules. (11)
Worship the Curved-Trunked one, the Single-Tusked one, the Big-Bellied one, the Elephant-Faced one, then the one called the Pot-Bellied one, the Fierce one, and the King of Obstacles. (12)
Then, at the tips of the petals, one should worship the one of smoke-colored hue, followed by the gods of the cardinal directions <note>Lokapalas</note> and their weapons; thus, one should worship the deity. (13)
The practitioner who has perfected the mantra should perform the rituals prescribed in the <term>kalpa</term> <gloss>scriptural manual</gloss>. One should propitiate the Leader of Hosts daily with pure water. (14)
One should perform the rite of forty-four and four hundred <note>444 repetitions</note> without lethargy. A man shall attain more than his heart's desire before the completion of the cycle. (15)
A burnt offering <note>homa</note> made with coconuts on the fourth lunar day brings wealth. Starting from the first day of the bright fortnight, a wise man should perform this daily. (16)
Until the fourth day, he should offer four hundred oblations using coconuts, parched grain, fried rice, and sesame, respectively. By doing so, he becomes like a master of all beings. (17)
A burnt offering with sesame and rice brings wealth and control over others. An offering of fried rice mixed with sweets grants a wife. (18)
By this method, a maiden obtains the desired bridegroom. A burnt offering with ghee-soaked oblations secures for men what they seek. (19)
A burnt offering performed at night for four days using fried rice mixed with curd creates great affection and makes the invisible visible forever. (20)

स्वभमदन्तं प्रतिचिन्त्य मौम्बदााक्रोष्टुकामः श्रियमातनोतु
॥ १४८ ॥
विघ्नार्गलानां विनिपाटनार्थं यं नारिकेलैः कदलीफलान्यैः ।
प्रतारयन्तो मदवारणास्यं प्रापुर्नराऽभीष्टमहं भजे तम् ॥१४९॥
यत्नैर्नेकबहुभिस्तपोभिराराध्यमाद्यं गजराजवक्त्रम् ।
स्तुत्यानया ये विधिना स्तुवन्ति ते सर्वलक्ष्मौनिधयो भवन्ति
॥ १५० ॥
इति सारदातिलके त्रयोदशः पटलः ।

---

->चतुर्दशः पटलः ।<-

अथोच्यते चन्द्रमसो मनुः सर्वसमृद्धिदः ।
खड्गस्थो भृगुविन्दुमनूतसमन्वितः ॥ १ ॥
सोमाय हृदयान्तोऽयं मन्त्रः प्रोक्तः षडक्षरः ।
ऋषिरुक्तो भृगुश्छन्दः पङ्क्तिः सोमोऽस्य देवता ॥ २ ॥
दीर्घभाजा स्वबीजेन मनोरङ्गक्रिया मता ॥ ३ ॥
कर्पूरस्फटिकावदातममिशं पूर्णेन्दुविम्बाननं
मुक्तादामविभूषितेन वपुषा निर्मूलयन्तं तमः ।
हस्ताभ्यां कुमुदं वरञ्च दधतं लीलाल्कोल्लासितं
स्वस्याङ्कस्थमगोदिताश्रयगुणं सोमं सुधाब्धिं भजे ॥ ४ ॥
वसुलक्षं जपेन्मन्त्रं साधको विजितेन्द्रियः ।
षट्सहस्रं प्रजुहुयात् पायसेन ससर्पिषा ॥ ५ ॥
सोमान्तं पूजिते पीठे पूजयेद्रोहिणीपतिम् ।
अङ्गानि केशरैस्तुष्टैः पत्रमध्यगाः ॥ ६ ॥
रोहिणी कृत्तिका भूयो रेवती भरणी पुनः ।
रात्रिरार्द्रा तथा ज्योत्स्ना मुक्ताहारसमप्रभाः ॥ ७ ॥

...may the one who wishes to invoke the Elephant-faced one increase his prosperity. (148) I worship that Elephant-faced one, whom men, leading him with coconuts and bananas, used to remove the bolts of obstacles, and thus obtained their desires. (149) Those who praise with this hymn and method the primal Elephant-faced one, who is to be worshipped through many diligent austerities, become the repositories of all wealth. (150) Thus ends the thirteenth chapter in the <term>Sarada Tilaka</term>.

---

->Fourteenth Chapter.<-

Now the mantra of the Moon is spoken, which grants all prosperity. It is in the sword, joined with the Bhrigu <note>śa</note> and the nasal point <note>m</note>. (1) The mantra ending in "heart" <note>namah</note> for Soma is stated as a six-syllable mantra: "Om to Soma." <note>original: "Om Somāya namah"</note> The sage is Bhrigu, the meter is <term>Pankti</term>, and the deity is Soma. (2) The limb-ritual for the mantra is considered to be done with one's own seed syllable joined with a long vowel. (3)

I worship Soma, the ocean of nectar, who is white as camphor and crystal, whose face is the orb of the full moon, who destroys darkness with a body decorated with strings of pearls, who holds a blue lotus and a boon in his hands, who is adorned with playful marks, and who has the qualities of the support of the gods in his own lap. (4) The seeker, having conquered the senses, should chant the mantra eight hundred thousand times and offer six thousand <term>payasa</term> <gloss>rice-milk pudding</gloss> with clarified butter. (5) On the throne worshipped by Soma and the rest, one should worship the Lord of Rohini. The limbs are to be worshipped with filaments in the middle of the petals. (6) Rohini, Krittika, Revati, and Bharani, Night, Ardra, and Moonlight, having the splendor of a pearl necklace. (7)

विंशः पटलः । २१४

रौद्रपिङ्गलनामानौ द्वौ श्मशानाद्भवावुभौ ।
दृढकर्णौ भङ्गरिटिसुदीर्घामर्चयेत् पुनः ॥ १२४ ॥
आमर्दकमहाकालौ कोषपालान् यजेत्ततः ।
कुम्भवर्षमत्यकाख्यं भल्लाटं जातहारकम् ॥ १२५ ॥
इन्द्रादिकान् लोकपालान् सायुधान् प्रयजेत्ततः ।
धूपदीपादिभिर्देवं प्रोषयित्वा महेश्वरम् ॥ १२६ ॥
पञ्चक्रूरान्वसा चाज्ये ततो भूतबलिं हरेत् ।
एवं पूजादिभिः सिद्धे मन्त्रे मन्त्रविदांवरः ॥ १२७ ॥
नाशयेत् सकलान् भूतान् कृत्याग्रहमहाभयान् ।
आदेशं तस्य कुर्वन्ति भूता भीता महात्मनः ॥ १२८ ॥
बहुना किमिहोक्तेन मन्त्रेणानेन भूतले ।
सदृशो नास्ति मन्त्रोऽन्यो भूतनिग्रहसाधनः ॥ १२९ ॥
इति सारदातिलके ऊनविंशः पटलः ।

---

विंशः पटलः ।

अथाभ्याख्ये विधिवद् घोरास्त्रमनुमुत्तमम् ।
यस्य संस्कारादेव सर्वे नश्यन्त्युपद्रवाः ॥ १ ॥
मायास्फुरहयं भूयः प्रस्फुरहितयं ततः ।
घोरघोरतरेत्यन्ते तनुरूपपदं पुनः ॥ २ ॥
चटयुग्मं तदन्ते स्यात् प्रचटितयं ततः ।
करयुगं रमदन्दं ततो वज्ञयुगं पुनः ॥ ३ ॥
घातय द्वितयं वर्मफडन्तः समुदीरितः ।
एकपञ्चाशदवर्णोऽयमघोरास्त्रमहामनुः ॥ ४ ॥
अघोरस्य मुनिः प्रोक्तश्छन्दस्त्रिष्टुबुदाहृतम् ।
अघोरमन्त्रः सन्दिष्टो देवता मन्त्रवित्तमैः ॥ ५ ॥

# Twentieth Chapter.

Twentieth Chapter. 214

(124) One should worship the two named Rudra-Pingala, born from the cremation ground, the firm-eared, the broken-toothed, and the very long one again. (125) Then worship the treasure-guardians named Amardaka and Mahakala. Then worship Kumbhavarsha, Atyaka, Bhallata, and Jataharaka. (126) Then worship the Lokapalas starting from Indra, equipped with their weapons. (127) Having satisfied the Great Lord with incense, lamps, and other offerings, (128) then make a <term>bhuta-bali</term> <gloss>offering to spirits</gloss> with the five cruel ones mixed with fat and ghee. Thus, when the mantra is perfected through worship and other acts, the master of mantras (129) shall destroy all ghosts, spirits, and great fears of sorcery. Terrified, the spirits do the bidding of that great-souled one. (130) What more is there to say? On this earth, there is no other mantra equal to this one for subduing spirits.

Thus ends the Nineteenth Chapter of the Sharada Tilaka.

Twentieth Chapter.

Now, the method for the excellent Aghora-Weapon mantra, by the very initiation of which all obstacles are destroyed. (2) The "Maya," followed by the quivering "Haya," then the double quivering "Hita," then "Ghora-Ghora-Tara," followed by the "Tanu-Rupa" word again. (3) Then the double "Chata," then the double "Prachata," then the double "Kara," the "Rama-Danda," then the double "Vajra." (4) "Ghataya" twice, and "Varmaphat" is declared at the end. This is the fifty-one syllable great mantra of the Aghora-Weapon. (5) The seer of the Aghora is declared; the meter is said to be Trishtubh. The Aghora mantra and its deity have been taught by those best at knowing mantras.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the 64 non-dual Bhairava-tantras. Having established the number 64 by multiplying the eight Vasus (8x8), the text now explains the metaphysical process by which the other four faces of Shiva—each containing 16 divisions—merge into the South (Bhairava) face to create the 64-fold non-dual system.</meta>

### [Verse 18] First Chapter ###

->**Page 41**<-

When the other four faces, which consist of sixteen divisions, are simultaneously dissolved within, then through their mutual combination, there arise the **sixty-four** <term>Bhairavabheda|The sixty-four non-dual divisions of the Bhairava scriptures</term> where non-duality is primary. As it has been said:

> “That which is at the end, the **Right Face** <note>original: "dakṣiṇaṃ" - In this tradition, the South face of Shiva is also the "Right" face, associated with the fierce form of Bhairava and the heart center</note>, relating to the heart, is considered the phallus of the supreme heart.
> Even that is overflowing with the entire creation drawn within it.
> Because it performs the dissolution of everything, it is **black** <note>original: "kṛṣṇaṃ" - The color black signifies the absorption of all colors and the dissolution of the objective world</note>, wearing the form of darkness.
> It consists of swallowing the luminous portions of the Maya-born world <term>Māyīya|Relating to Maya, the power that creates the illusion of separation or duality</term> that cause the sense of difference.
> Into that [South Face], the other four faces become dissolved:
> those desiring to manifest, those already manifested, those desiring to conceal, and those already concealed.
> In this way, simultaneously, these sixteen divisions
> enter the Right, the creative, the heartfelt, the independent, and the auspicious [Face of Shiva].
> That scripture is simultaneously named after **Bhairava**, consisting of **eight times eight** <note>original: "aṣṭāṣṭaka" - 64</note> parts.”

This has been stated in detail in the **Srikanthi-Samhita** <note>A foundational scripture often cited by Abhinavagupta for the classification of Tantras</note>, beginning with their specific names. As it says:

> “I shall briefly speak of another [teaching] sung by the **Supreme Lord** <term>Parameṣṭhin|A title for the highest deity, usually Shiva in this context</term>.
> I shall speak of it in its divisions, sixty-four in total.”

***

**Manuscript Variations:**
*   Line 3: Manuscript Ga reads: “And so it is said,” in this manner.
*   Line 12: Manuscript Ga reads: “The scripture consisting of eight times eight.”
*   Line 14: Manuscript Ga reads: “As follows.”
*   Line 16: Manuscript Ka reads: “The sixty-four divisions.”

<sig>6</sig>

<summary>This page explains the metaphysical origin of the 64 non-dual Bhairava scriptures. It describes how the other four "faces" or modes of revelation dissolve into the South face (Bhairava), which represents the "Heart" and the dissolution of all dualistic differences into a single, black, all-consuming reality.</summary>

<keywords>Bhairavabheda, Srikanthi, South Face, Non-duality, Heart, Dissolution, Shiva, 64 Tantras</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the analysis of the word "I" (mām) used by Krishna in the Bhagavad Gītā. Abhinavagupta is arguing that this "I" does not refer to a limited historical figure, but to the universal Pure Awareness that underlies all existence. He now addresses the apparent paradox of how a single, non-dual Awareness can simultaneously be the worshipper and the deity being worshipped.</meta>

### Light on the Tantras <note>original: "Śrī Tantrāloka"</note>
<page-num>172</page-num>
<header>Light on the Tantras</header>

->By the two words "Enjoyer" and "Lord,"<-
->He is expressed as both the object of worship and the worshipper. || 132 ||<-

In this context—meaning within the text of the *Gītā*—the intention is to explain **undivided pure awareness** <term>bodha-mātra</term> alone. For this reason, it is said that the "grasper" or the "subject who reflects" <note>original: "parāmraṣṭā"</note> is a designator for awareness in its absolute state. Indeed, there is no possibility of a second thing existing outside of **Light** <term>prakāśa</term> that could serve as a counter-correlate to be excluded. This is because any such thing would be subject to the dilemma of being either "manifest" or "unmanifest"—if it is manifest, it is already part of the Light; if it is unmanifest, it is nothing at all. 

However, the "I-awareness" <term>ahaṃ-vimarśa</term> that identifies with the body, such as in the thought "I am thin," is merely a **conceptual construct** <term>vikalpa</term>. This is because it relies on excluding other things; the "I" of the body is only defined in opposition to "others" or "objects" that are not the body. 

Now, a question is raised: If Awareness alone exists as a single reality without any opponent or "other," then how can the distinction between the **object of worship** <term>yājya</term> and the **worshipper** <term>yaṣṭṛ</term>—found in phrases like "they worship Me"—be considered ultimately real? 

Anticipating this doubt, the author says: *By the two words "Enjoyer" and "Lord"* and so on. The core idea is that **Awareness** <term>bodha</term> itself flashes forth or manifests in the form of both the subject and the object. As it is said in that very text <note>the Bhagavad Gītā, 9.24</note>:

> "I am indeed the enjoyer and also the Lord of all sacrifices." 

|| 132 ||

But then, another doubt arises: How can that which is "one" and that which "consists of both" be reconciled? Anticipating this, he says:

<summary>Abhinavagupta explains that the divine "I" in the Bhagavad Gītā represents universal Awareness, which transcends the ego. He argues that the apparent duality between the worshipper and the deity is actually a single Awareness manifesting as both roles simultaneously.</summary>
<keywords>Pure Awareness, Prakasha, Vimarsha, Vikalpa, Worshipper and Worshipped, Bhagavad Gita, Non-duality, Enjoyer, Lord</keywords>

<meta>This page continues Abhinavagupta’s argument regarding the nature of liberation. Having just dismissed the dualist view that different spiritual methods lead to different types of salvation, he now uses a logical analogy involving a broken pot to demonstrate that the end of "impurity" is the same regardless of what triggers it.</meta>

<page-num>201</page-num>
<header>Verse 166 ] The First Daily Lesson</header>

...en universal Consciousness? Therefore, since there is no difference in the underlying reality, what possible difference could there be in liberation <term>mokṣa; the final state of spiritual freedom</term>, which is the ultimate result?
[165 continued]

An objection is raised:

->**"And that attainment is directly through the means..."**<-

Wait, since it has been stated in passages such as this that there is a "multiplicity of direct means," how can there *not* be a difference in the result based on the difference in those means? <note>The objector argues that if the "causes" (the methods) are diverse, the "effect" (the goal) must also be diverse.</note>

Anticipating this doubt, the author says:

->**Through the destruction of impurity and its power,**<-
->**and the removal of concealment—**<-
->**even if the causes vary, the result is not different,**<-
->**just like the various ways a pot may be destroyed. [166]**<-

Even in cases where a real relationship of cause and effect exists, there is no difference in the result—such as the destruction of impurity <term>mala; the spiritual "grime" or limitation that binds the soul</term> and its power—even if the cause, such as initiation <term>dīkṣā</term>, varies. This is because, although initiation may differ based on the specific power <term>kalā</term>, principle <term>tattva</term>, or cosmic realm <term>bhuvana</term> being addressed, the final result itself remains the same. 

To illustrate this: a pot can be smashed by a hammer, a hand, hitting a wall, or colliding with another pot. Despite these different "means" or causes of destruction, the resulting state—the "destruction" or "disappearance" of the pot—is exactly the same in every case. <note>This is a classic logical example in Indian philosophy to show that different actions can lead to an identical state of absence.</note> 

Therefore, it is by no means a universal rule that a difference in cause must necessitate a difference in the result. Where, however...

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the nature of the Absolute as the "Light of Consciousness." Having established in the previous verse that the Absolute shines as the self of all things, Abhinavagupta now describes the internal experience of this state and cites the Triśirobhairava Tantra to support the idea that the Absolute is always "pregnant" with its own creative Power.</meta>

# The Holy Tantrāloka #

<page-num>26</page-num>
<header>The Holy Tantrāloka</header>

...ed. However, for those whose mental fluctuations have settled into a state of pure stillness <term>kalpavṛtti</term> <note>the state where the churning of conceptual thought has ceased</note>, this reality shines as something that surpasses everything else. It is perceived as a dense, concentrated mass of supreme bliss and aesthetic wonder <term>camatkāra</term> <note>the "aha!" moment of consciousness recognizing its own infinite nature</note> that arises from one's own direct experience. This is why it was said in the previous verse that "this state is the incomparable Beyond." <note>original: "kimapyetadanuttaram"</note> ॥ 31 ॥

This truth has not only been stated here in this text, but has been declared elsewhere in the scriptures as well. Thus, the author says:

->In the venerable *Triśirobhairava Tantra*,<-
->the nature of supreme knowledge is declared:<-
->"The supreme state is 'pregnant with Power'<-
->through that Power which resides within its very womb."<- ॥ 32 ॥

The intention here is that the Blessed Lord spoke of this "nature of supreme knowledge" in order to resolve the question asked by the Goddess: "O Lord, how is supreme knowledge attained?" He then quotes the passage beginning with "through that Power." This "supreme state" is "pregnant with Power" <term>śaktigarbham</term> <note>literally 'having Power in the womb,' meaning the Absolute contains all potential within itself</note>. Here, "Power" refers to that which is called by such names as "Absolute Freedom" <term>svātantrya</term> and "Reflective Awareness" <term>vimarśa</term>. This Power is the "womb" or the "essence" of the supreme state.

Furthermore, this Power is not something separate or external to the Absolute. This is why the verse says "through that Power which resides within its very womb." Because of that very Power called Freedom, the "womb"—which refers to the inner reality or the state of being one with the Subject <term>pramātṛ-aikātmya</term> <note>the state where the individual experiencer realizes they are identical with the universal Knower</note>—exists in its highest possible limit. It is characterized by this Power, which is the Absolute's own true nature. If it were otherwise, the Absolute would not possess the quality of being "supreme" at all. As it has been said:

---

<note>Line 7: In manuscript 'Ka', the reading is 'residing within the womb' [garbhāntavāsinyā] instead of 'existing within'.</note>

<summary>This page explains that the Absolute is experienced as concentrated bliss (camatkāra) and cites the Triśirobhairava Tantra to define the supreme state as being "pregnant with Power" (śaktigarbha).</summary>
<keywords>Anuttara (the Beyond), Camatkāra (rapture), Triśirobhairava Tantra, Śakti (Power), Svātantrya (Freedom), Vimarśa (Reflective Awareness), Pramātṛ (Subject)</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the technical and ritual instructions for the "Protective Armor" (Kavacha) begun on the previous page. It transitions from the general praise of the teacher to the specific application of sacred mantras and the relationship between the Guru and the disciple in the process of spiritual liberation.</meta>

# The Ritual of the Teacher’s Armor

<gloss>The <term>Savitri Mantra<note>The Gayatri Mantra, a highly revered Vedic chant for spiritual enlightenment</note></term> along with the life-breaths; the descent and the falling away of obstacles.</gloss>

Ignorance is a grasping force, yet through its destruction, a greater capacity for hearing and feeling arises within you this day. <note>The text contrasts "Avidya" (ignorance/illusion) with the "Vidya" (knowledge) gained through the Guru</note>. This expansion is detailed; as you have become a witness to it, perform it here. Through the movement of the heart, the intelligence is prepared for the <term>First Union<gloss>Adyoga</gloss></term>.

<column-break/>

<insert>40</insert>
Regarding the desires of the body and the fame of the descendants of Manu, he became the master of the <term>Three Worlds<note>The Triloka: usually defined as Earth, the Atmosphere, and Heaven</note></term>. There are 108 such aspects. Having ordained his own <term>Disciple<gloss>Shishya</gloss></term>, the teacher is asked: the speech has arrived. The journey of deliberation and sacrifice; the expert mind has moved beyond doubt, becoming a master of speech. Whatever is cast aside from the state of decay, the son has presented to the <term>Master Teacher<gloss>Acharya</gloss></term>.

<column-break/>

Now today, in the house of the **Guru**, in such a manner, the universal power and the weapons are invoked. <note>The manuscript contains several ritual syllables here: Kahuri, Banu, Kohi, and Lahi</note>. Rising with the <term>Pinaka bow<note>The specific bow belonging to Lord Shiva</note></term> in hand, the son of the protector of the gods is capable of forgiveness. May my <term>Spiritual Attainment<gloss>Siddhi</gloss></term> be realized; whatever was left undone is now completed, even unto the <term>Cremation Ground<gloss>Shmashana</gloss></term> <note>In this context, the cremation ground represents the place where the ego is destroyed and final liberation is sought</note>.

<summary>This page describes the transmission of sacred knowledge from the Guru to the disciple, highlighting the removal of ignorance and the mastery of the three worlds. It concludes with an invocation of Shiva’s power and the completion of spiritual tasks in the sacred space of the cremation ground.</summary>
<keywords>Savitri Mantra, Guru, Shishya, Three Worlds, 108, Acharya, Shiva, Shmashana, spiritual liberation</keywords>

न । अ॒हम् । या॒तुम् । सह॑सा । न । द्व॒येन॑ । ऋ॒तम् । स॒पा॒मि॒ । अ॒रु॒षस्य॑ । वृष्णः॑ ॥ २ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

ऋतं स्तोत्रं हे चिकित्वो जानन्नग्ने त्वं ऋतं मया क्रियमाणमिदं स्तोत्रं चिकिद्धि । जानीहि ॥ कित ज्ञाने । जुहोत्यादिः । लोटि रूपं । इदिति पूरणः । ऋतमिति पदस्य परस्मिन्नमञ्चिते विद्यमानेऽपि छांदसत्वात्परांगवद्भावाभावः ॥ किंच पूर्वीर्बह्वीर्ऋतस्योदकस्य धारास्तस्य पोषणार्थमुत्पादयितुमनुवृंधि । मेघाननुविध्य । सहसा बलेन युक्तोऽहं यातुं कर्मणां नाशकरीं हिंसां न सपामि । न स्पृशामि । न करोमीति यावत् । द्वयेन च सत्यानृताभ्यां यत्किंचिद्वैदिकं कृत्यं न सपामि ॥ षप समवाय इति धातुः ॥ किंतु अरुषस्य रोचमानस्य वृष्णः कामानां वर्षितुस्तव ऋतं स्तोत्रमेव सपामि ॥

---

->॥ अथ तृतीया ॥<-

## Hymn Text

कया॑ नो अग्ने ऋतयन्नृ॒तेन॑ भु॒वो नर्वेदा उच॒थस्य॒ नव्य॑: ।
वेदा॑ मे दे॒व ऋ॑तु॒पा ऋ॑तू॒नां नाहं पतिं॑ सनि॒तुर॑स्य रा॒यः ॥ ३ ॥

<vocab>
अग्नि (Agni), ऋत (Rita - Truth/Cosmic Order), वृषभ (Vrishabha - Bull/Showering deity), असुर (Asura - Powerful), घृत (Ghrita - Ghee), मन्म (Manma - Prayer/Thought), गिर (Gira - Speech/Hymn), चिकित्वस् (Chikitvas - Wise/Knowing)
</vocab>
pages.translation:
<meta>This page transitions from the general praises of Agni in the 11th hymn to the 12th hymn of the fifth Mandala. The 12th hymn, also dedicated to Agni, focuses on the concept of 'Rita'—the cosmic order or truth—and the worshipper's rejection of falsehood and violence. The previous page concluded the commentary on Verse 5 of the 11th hymn, comparing hymns to rivers filling the ocean.</meta>

[Ma. 5. A. 1. Su. 12.] || Fourth Book || 309

->॥ Now the First Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**For the great Agni, worthy of sacrifice, the showerer of Truth, the powerful Lord, I bring this prayer. Like well-purified ghee in the sacrifice, I offer this forward-facing hymn to the Bull [Agni] into his mouth. ॥ 1 ॥**

**Prasada-patha (Word-for-word):**
**For | Agni | the great | worthy of sacrifice | of Truth | the showerer | for the powerful Lord | prayer |**
**Ghee | like | in the sacrifice | in the mouth | well-purified | speech/hymn | I bring | for the Bull | forward-facing ॥ 1 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

For the **great** <note>original: "bṛhate"</note> one, great because of his excessive power; for the one **worthy of sacrifice** <note>original: "yajñiyāya"</note>; for the **showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣṇe"</note> or pourer of **Truth** <note>original: "ṛtasya"</note>, which here refers to water (rain), as "Rita" is listed among the names for water; for the **powerful Lord** <note>original: "asurāya"</note> or the strong one (the word *asura* is formed with the suffix *uran* from the root *as*).

To the **Bull** <note>original: "vṛṣabhāya"</note>, the one who showers desires—to Agni—I **bring** <note>original: "prabhare"</note> or offer a **prayer** <note>original: "manma"</note>, which is the means of knowledge, and a **speech** <note>original: "giram"</note> in the form of a hymn that is **forward-facing** <note>original: "pratīcīm"</note> or directed toward him. How? Like **ghee** <note>original: "ghṛtaṃ na"</note> that is **well-purified** <note>original: "supūtaṃ"</note>, properly prepared and offered into the **mouth** <note>original: "āsye"</note> during a **sacrifice** <note>original: "yajñe"</note>. The meaning is: just as ghee poured into the mouth is pleasing, I offer a hymn that is equally pleasing.

---

->॥ Now the Second Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**O Wise One, you know the Truth; recognize the Truth! Release the many streams of Truth. I do not [approach] violence with force, nor with duality [falsehood]; I adhere to the Truth of the bright Showerer. ॥ 2 ॥**

**Padapatha:**
**Truth | O Wise One | Truth | indeed | recognize | of Truth | streams | along | release | many |**
**Not | I | violence/sorcery | with force | not | with duality | Truth | I adhere to | of the bright | of the showerer ॥ 2 ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O **Wise** <note>original: "cikityo"</note> or knowing Agni, you who know the **Truth** <note>original: "ṛtaṃ"</note> in the form of the hymn, **recognize** <note>original: "cikiddhi"</note> or take notice of this Truth, this hymn being performed by me. (The root is *kit* "to know," in the imperative mood). The word *it* is a filler. Even though the word *rita* is followed by another word, it does not undergo certain phonetic changes due to Vedic license.

Furthermore, **release** <note>original: "anutṛndhi"</note> or set free the **many** <note>original: "pūrvīḥ"</note> **streams** <note>original: "dhārāḥ"</note> of **Truth** <note>original: "ṛtasya"</note> (water/rain) for the sake of nourishment, having pierced through the clouds. **I** <note>original: "aham"</note>, though endowed with **force** <note>original: "sahasā"</note> or strength, **do not adhere to** <note>original: "na sapāmi"</note>—that is, I do not touch or perform—**violence** <note>original: "yātum"</note> which destroys rituals. Nor do I perform any Vedic act with **duality** <note>original: "dvayena"</note>, which refers to a mixture of truth and untruth. (The root *ṣap* means to connect or involve). Rather, **I adhere to** the **Truth** or the hymn of you, the **bright** <note>original: "aruṣasya"</note> or shining **Showerer** <note>original: "vṛṣṇaḥ"</note> of desires.

---

->॥ Now the Third Verse ॥<-

## Hymn Text

**By what Truth, O Agni, being truthful through Truth, do you become for us the knower of this new hymn? The god who knows the seasons, the protector of seasons, knows me; I [do] not [know] the lord of this giving wealth... ॥ 3 ॥**

<vocab>
**Agni**: The Fire-god, messenger between gods and humans.
**Rita**: The Cosmic Order, Truth, or sometimes refers to the sacrificial water/rain.
**Vrishabha**: Literally 'Bull,' used here as a title for a deity who showers blessings or rain.
**Asura**: In the Rig Veda, this often means a powerful lord or divine being (before it later came to mean 'demon').
**Ghrita**: Clarified butter (ghee), the primary offering in Vedic fire sacrifices.
**Manma**: A prayer, thought, or inspired meditation.
**Gira**: Speech or hymns of praise.
**Chikitvas**: One who is wise, conscious, or all-knowing.
</vocab>

<summary>This page contains the first three verses of Hymn 12 in the fifth book of the Rig Veda, where the poet invokes Agni as the guardian of 'Rita' (Truth/Cosmic Order). The text emphasizes the purity of the hymn, comparing it to clarified butter, and the worshipper's commitment to truth over falsehood or violence.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Rita (Truth), Vedic sacrifice, Sayana commentary, Mandala 5, Ghee offerings, Asura, Bull (Vrishabha)</keywords>

<meta>
This page contains the conclusion of the commentary for Rig Veda Mandala 6, Sukta 15, Verse 5, and the complete text (Samhita and Pada patha) with commentary for Verse 6. The header indicates this is part of the Fourth Ashtaka. 
</meta>

## Hymn Text

पाव॒कया॑ । यः । चि॒तय॑न्त्या । कृ॒पा । क्षाम॑न् । रु॒रु॒चे । उ॒षस॑: । न । भा॒नुना॑ ।
तूर्व॑न् । न । याम॑न् । एत॑शस्य । नु । रणे॑ । आ । यः । घृ॒णे । न । त॒तृ॒षा॒णः । अ॒जर॑: ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

योऽग्निः **पावकया** शोधयित्र्या **चितयन्त्या** चेतयन्त्या प्रज्ञापयन्त्या **कृपा** दीप्त्या **क्षामन्** भूम्यां **रुरुचे** दीप्यते । **उषसो न भानुना** । यथोषसः प्रकाशेन भासते तद्वत् । अपि च **यामन्** यामनि संयामे **तूर्वन्** शत्रून् हिंसन् पुरुष इव **एतशस्य** तत्संज्ञस्य ऋषे **रणे** सूर्येण सह संयामे सहायार्थं योऽग्निः **नु** क्षिप्रम् **आघृणे** आदी प्यते । **प्रैतशं सूर्ये पस्पृधानं** । ऋग्वे० १. ६१. १५ । इति निगमांतरं । नूनं सर्वे देवास्तस्य साहाय्यमकार्षुः । यश्च **ततृषाणः** तृषितः प्रभावेन सर्वभक्षणशीलो **ऽजरो** जरारहितश्च भवति तं देवमंजस इति पूर्वस्यामृचि संबंधः ॥

-> ॥ इति चतुर्थस्य पंचमे सप्तदशो वर्गः ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ अथ षष्ठी ॥ <-

अ॒ग्निम॑ग्निं वः॒ समि॑धा दुवस्यत प्रि॒यंप्रि॑यम् वो॒ अति॑थिं गृणीषणिं ।
उप॑ वः गी॒र्भिर्अ॒मृतं॑ विवासत दे॒वो दे॒वेषु॑ वनते॒ हि वार्यं॑ दे॒वो दे॒वेषु॑ वनते॒ हि
नो॒ दुव॑: ॥ ६ ॥

**Pada-patha:**
अ॒ग्निम्ऽअ॑ग्निम् । वः॒ । सम्ऽइ॑धा । दु॒व॒स्य॒त॒ । प्रि॒यम्ऽप्रि॑यम् । वः॒ । अति॑थिम् । गृ॒णी॒षणि॑म् ।
उप॑ । वः॒ । गीः॒ऽभिः । अ॒मृत॑म् । वि॒वा॒स॒त॒ । दे॒वः । दे॒वेषु॑ । व॒न॒ते॒ । हि । वार्य॑म् । दे॒वः ।
दे॒वेषु॑ । व॒न॒ते॒ । हि । नः॒ । दुव॑: ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

हे अस्मदीयाः स्तोतारो **वः** यूयं **प्रियं प्रियं** अत्यंतं प्रियं **वः** युष्माकम् **अतिथिम्** अतिथिवत्पूज्यं **गृणीषणिं** शब्दनीयं स्तुत्यम् **अग्निमग्निं** अग्निमेव । नान्यं देवमित्यर्थः । **समिधा** समिंधनेन समिद्भिर्वा **दुवस्यत** । परिचरत । यद्वा गृणीषणीति सप्तम्यंतं । गृणीषणि स्तोत्रे विषयतया वर्तमानं । अपि च **वः** यूयम् **अमृतम्** अमरणम् अग्निं **गीर्भिः** स्तुतिभिरुपेत्य **विवासत** । परिचरत । **हि** यस्मात् **देवेषु** मध्ये **देवो** दानादिगुणयुक्तोऽग्निर् **वार्यं** वरणीयं समिदादिकं **वनते** संभजते । **हि** यस्माच्च **देवेषु** मध्ये **देवो** ऽग्निः **नः** अस्माकं **दुवः** परिचरणं **वनते** संभजते तस्माद्दुवस्यतेत्यन्वयः ॥

दशमेऽहन्याग्निमारुते **समिद्धम्** इति तृचो जातवेदस्यनिविद्धानार्थः । सूचितं च । **समिद्धमग्निं समिधा गिरा गृण** इति तृचश्च । आ० ८. १२ । इति ॥

<vocab>
अग्नि (Agni), समिध् (Samidh - fuel/wood), अतिथि (Atithi - guest), वार्य (Varya - desirable/precious), दुवस्यत (Duvasyata - worship/serve), एतश (Etasha - a mythical horse/sage), उषस् (Ushas - dawn), जातवेदस् (Jatavedas - epithet of Agni)
</vocab>
pages.translation:
<meta>This page continues the commentary on the 15th Hymn of the 6th Mandala of the Rig Veda. It concludes the explanation for Verse 5 and provides the full text and commentary for Verse 6. The focus remains on Agni's dual nature as a cosmic light and a ritual fire.</meta>

## Hymn Text

**By the purifying [light], by the awakening light, he has shone upon the earth like the Dawn with her radiance; as if overcoming [enemies] in a march, [he helps] in the battle of Etasha; he who shines quickly, as if thirsty, the ageless one. ॥ ५ ॥**

**Purifying | who | awakening | by light | on the earth | has shone | of the dawn | like | with radiance |**
**Overcoming | like | in a march | of Etasha | quickly | in battle | hither | who | in heat/shining | like | thirsty | ageless ॥ ५ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That Agni, with his **purifying** <note>original: "pāvakayā," meaning cleansing or sanctifying</note> and **awakening** <note>original: "citayantyā," that which makes one conscious or bestows wisdom</note> **light** <note>original: "kṛpā," beauty or luster</note>, **has shone** <note>original: "ruruce"</note> upon the **earth** <note>original: "kṣāman"</note>. **Like the Dawn with her radiance**—just as the Dawn shines with her own light, so does he. Furthermore, in a **march** <note>original: "yāman"</note> or a conflict, like a man **overcoming** <note>original: "tūrvan"</note> or striking down his enemies, Agni **quickly** <note>original: "nu"</note> **shines** <note>original: "āghṛṇe"</note> to assist in the **battle** <note>original: "raṇe"</note> of the sage named **Etasha** <note>original: "etaśasya"</note> against the Sun. *“And Etasha contended with the Sun”* <note>original: "praitaśaṃ sūrye paspṛdhānaṃ," quoting Rig Veda 1.61.15</note>—this is another Vedic citation for the same story. Surely all the gods provided him assistance there. And he who is **thirsty** <note>original: "tatṛṣāṇaḥ," meaning one who by his power tends to consume everything</note> and **ageless** <note>original: "ajaraḥ," free from decay</note>—this refers to that god described in the previous verse.

-> ॥ Thus ends the seventeenth section of the fifth chapter of the fourth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**Serve Agni after Agni with fuel; [serve] your very dear guest, who is to be praised. Approach the immortal one with your songs; for he, the god among gods, accepts the precious gift; for he, the god among gods, accepts our service. ॥ ६ ॥**

**Pada-patha:**
**Agni | Agni | your | with fuel | serve | dear | dear | your | guest | who is to be praised |**
**Towards | your | with songs | the immortal | approach/serve | the god | among the gods | accepts | indeed | the precious | the god |**
**among the gods | accepts | indeed | our | service ॥ ६ ॥**

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

O our singers/praisers, **your** <note>original: "vaḥ"</note>—that is, you all—**serve** <note>original: "duvasyata," worship or attend to</note> **Agni after Agni** <note>original: "agnimagnim," indicating each individual fire or every ritual occasion</note>, and no other god. He is **your** very **dear** <note>original: "priyam priyam"</note> **guest** <note>original: "atithim," to be honored like a guest in the home</note> and **to be praised** <note>original: "gṛṇīṣaṇim," worthy of hymns</note>. Serve him **with fuel** <note>original: "samidhā," the act of kindling or with the sacrificial wood sticks</note>. Alternatively, "to be praised" could be interpreted as being the subject of the song itself. Furthermore, you all **approach and serve** <note>original: "vivāsata"</note> the **immortal** <note>original: "amṛtam"</note> Agni **with your songs** <note>original: "gīrbhiḥ"</note> or hymns. **For** <note>original: "hi"</note> among the **gods**, the **god** Agni, who possesses the quality of giving, **accepts** <note>original: "vanate," enjoys or partakes in</note> the **precious gift** <note>original: "vāryam," the desirable offerings like fuel and clarified butter</note>. **For** among the **gods**, the **god** Agni **accepts** <note>original: "vanate"</note> **our service** <note>original: "duvaḥ," our worshipful attendance</note>; therefore, the instruction is to "serve" him.

Regarding the ritual for the tenth day of the *Agni-maruta* ceremony, the triplet of verses beginning with **"Kindled"** <note>original: "samiddham"</note> serves as the invitation for the *Jatavedas* offering. As it is stated: *"The triplet 'Kindled is Agni, praise him with fuel and song'..."* <note>original: quoting the Ashvalayana Shrauta Sutra 8.12</note>.

<vocab>
**Agni**: The Fire God. | **Samidh**: Fuel or sacrificial wood. | **Atithi**: Guest (Agni is the guest of the house). | **Varya**: Desirable or precious offering. | **Duvasyata**: Worship or serve. | **Etasha**: A mythical horse or sage involved in a race with the Sun. | **Ushas**: The Goddess of Dawn. | **Jatavedas**: A common title for Agni meaning "knower of all births/beings."
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes verse 5, describing Agni's brilliance compared to the dawn and his aid in the myth of Etasha, and presents verse 6, which exhorts worshippers to serve Agni as a dear guest with fuel and hymns.</summary>
<keywords>Agni, Etasha, Dawn, sacrifice, ritual fuel, hospitality, immortality, Sayana's commentary</keywords>

<meta>This page contains the text and commentary (Sayanabhashya) for Rig Veda, Mandala 7, Sukta 4, verses 5, 6, and 7. The header indicates the location in the Ashtaka system: Ashtaka 5, Adhyaya 2, Varga 6. The hymn text for verse 5 is presented in Padapatha form at the top, followed by verses 6 and 7 in both Samhitapatha and Padapatha.</meta>

## Hymn Text

आ । यः । योनिं॑ । दे॒वऽकृ॑तं । ससा॑द । ऋ॒त्वा । हि । अ॒ग्निः । अ॒मृता॑न् । अ॒तारी॑त् ।
तं । ओष॑धीः । च॒ । व॒निन॑: । च॒ । गर्भं॑ । भूमिः॑ । च॒ । वि॒श्वऽधा॑यसं । बिभ॑र्ति ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

योऽग्निर्देवकृतं देवैः कल्पितं योनिं स्थानमाससाद अध्यास्ते । किमर्थं देवाः स्थानं कल्पयन्त्यग्नेरित्यत आह । हि यस्मात्कारणादग्निः ऋत्वा प्रज्ञयामृतान्देवानतारीत् । विश्वधायसं विश्वस्य धारकमोषधीरोषधयो वनिनश्च वृक्षाश्च गर्भं गर्भं सन्तं तं बिभ्रति । भूमिश्च बिभर्ति ॥ श्रुतमैव बिभर्तीति पदं बहुवचनानंतया विपरिणतं सदोषधीभिवनिनिभिश्च संबध्यते ॥

-> ॥ इति पंचमस्य द्वितीये पंचमो वर्गः ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ अथ षष्ठी ॥ <-

ईशे॒ ह्य॑ग्नि॒रमृत॑स्य॒ भूरे॑री॒शे रा॒यः सु॒वीर्य॑स्य दा॒तोः ।
मा त्वा॑ व॒यं स॑हसाव॒न्नवी॑रा॒ माप्स॑वः॒ परि॑ षदाम॒ मादु॑वः ॥ ६ ॥

ईशे॑ । हि । अ॒ग्निः । अ॒मृत॑स्य । भूरे॑: । ईशे॑ । रा॒यः । सु॒ऽवीर्य॑स्य । दा॒तोः ।
मा । त्वा॒ । व॒यम् । सह॑साऽवन् । अ॒वीरा॑: । मा । अ॒प्सवः॑ । परि॑ । स॒दाम॒ । मा । अ॒दुवः॑ ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

अमृतस्यान्नमुदकं वा ॥ द्वितीयार्थे षष्ठी ॥ भूरेरधिकं दातोर्दातुमग्नीरीशे । ईष्टे हि । सुवीर्यस्य शोभनवीर्ययुक्तं रायो धनं दातुमीशे । ईष्टे । अथ प्रत्यक्षस्तुतिः । सहसावन् हे बलवन्नग्ने वयं वसिष्ठा अवीराः पुत्रादिरहिताः संतो मा परिषद्दाम । मा पर्युपविशाम । अप्सवो रूपरहिताश्च संतो मा परिषद्दाम । तथा च यास्कः । अप्स इति रूपनामेति । अदुवः परिचरणहीनाश्च मा परिषद्दाम ॥

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ अथ सप्तमी ॥ <-

परि॑षद्यं॒ ह्य॑र॒णस्य॑ रे॒क्णो नित्य॑स्य रा॒यः पत॑यः स्याम ।
न शेपो॑ अग्ने अ॒न्यजा॑त॒मस्त्यचे॑तानस्य॒ मा प॒थो वि दुक्षः ॥ ७ ॥

परि॑ऽसद्यं । हि । अ॒र॒णस्य॑ । रे॒क्णः॑ । नित्य॑स्य । रा॒यः । पत॑यः । स्याम ।
न । शेषः॑ । अ॒ग्ने॒ । अ॒न्यऽजा॑तं । अ॒स्ति । अ॒चे॒तानस्य । मा । प॒थः । वि । दुक्षः ॥ ७ ॥

## Commentary (Sayana)

अरणस्यान्यस्य रेक्णो धनं परिषद्यं पर्याप्तं भवति हि । अतो नित्यस्यापुनर्देयस्य रायो धनस्य पतयः स्याम । यद्वा अरणस्य रेक्णो धनं परिषद्यं परिहर्तव्यं

## Hymn Text

**He who has sat in the source made by the gods; indeed, Agni has surpassed the immortals by his wisdom. The plants and the trees and the earth carry him, the supporter of all, like an embryo.** ॥ ५ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
आ (Toward/at) । यः (who) । योनिं॑ (source/place) । दे॒वऽकृ॑तं (god-made) । ससा॑द (has sat) । ऋ॒त्वा (by wisdom/intelligence) । हि (indeed) । अ॒ग्निः (Agni) । अ॒मृता॑न् (the immortals) । अ॒तारी॑त् (has crossed/surpassed) ।
तं (him) । ओष॑धीः (plants) । च॒ (and) । व॒निन॑: (trees) । च॒ (and) । गर्भं॑ (embryo) । भूमिः॑ (earth) । च॒ (and) । वि॒श्वऽधा॑यसं (all-supporting) । बिभ॑र्ति (carries) ॥ ५ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

That Agni who **has sat in** <note>original: "āsasāda"</note>—meaning occupies—the **source** <note>original: "yoniṃ"</note> or place **made by the gods** <note>original: "devakṛtaṃ"</note> or arranged by them. Why do the gods arrange a place for Agni? To this, the text says: **Indeed** <note>original: "hi"</note> because Agni **surpassed** <note>original: "atārīt"</note> the **immortal** <note>original: "amṛtān"</note> gods through his **wisdom** <note>original: "kratvā"</note> or intelligence. The **plants** <note>original: "oṣadhayaḥ"</note> and the **trees** <note>original: "vaninaśca"</note> carry him, the **supporter of all** <note>original: "viśvadhāyasaṃ"</note>, while he is an **embryo** <note>original: "garbhaṃ"</note>. The **earth** <note>original: "bhūmiśca"</note> also carries him. <note>Grammatical note: The word "carries" (bibharti) is seen here as being transformed into a plural sense to connect with the many subjects: plants and trees.</note>

-> ॥ This concludes the fifth group in the second chapter of the fifth book ॥ <-

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Sixth Verse ॥ <-

**For Agni is the lord of much immortality; he is the lord of giving wealth and good hero-strength. O mighty one, may we not sit around you without sons, without form, or without service.** ॥ ६ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
ईशे॑ (Rules/is lord) । हि (for) । अ॒ग्निः (Agni) । अ॒मृत॑स्य (of immortality) । भूरे॑: (of much) । ईशे॑ (rules) । रा॒यः (of wealth) । सु॒ऽवीर्य॑स्य (of good hero-strength) । दा॒तोः (of the giver) ।
मा (not) । त्वा॒ (you) । व॒यम् (we) । सह॑साऽवन् (O mighty one) । अ॒वीरा॑: (without sons/heroes) । मा (not) । अ॒प्सवः॑ (without form/beauty) । परि॑ (around) । स॒दाम॒ (may we sit) । मा (not) । अ॒दुवः॑ (without service) ॥ ६ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

Agni **rules** <note>original: "īṣṭe"</note> over **much** <note>original: "bhūreḥ"</note> **immortality** <note>original: "amṛtasya"</note>, which refers here to sacrificial food or water. <note>Grammatical note: The genitive case is used here in the sense of the objective case.</note> He is the lord and the **giver** <note>original: "dātoḥ"</note> of **wealth** <note>original: "rāyaḥ"</note> consisting of **excellent hero-strength** <note>original: "suvīryasya"</note> or power. Now follows a direct praise: **O mighty one** <note>original: "sahasāvan"</note>, O powerful Agni, may we, the clan of Vasistha, **not sit around** <note>original: "mā pariṣadāma"</note> you being **without sons** <note>original: "avīrāḥ"</note>—that is, lacking children and descendants. May we not sit around you **without form** <note>original: "apsavaḥ"</note>, meaning being devoid of beauty or status. As the ancient etymologist Yaska says: <gloss>The word "apsas" is a name for "form" (rūpa).</gloss> Also, may we not sit around you being **without service** <note>original: "aduvaḥ"</note>—meaning lacking in the performance of ritual service.

---

## Hymn Text

-> ॥ Now the Seventh Verse ॥ <-

**The wealth of a stranger is indeed to be avoided; let us be the masters of our own eternal wealth. O Agni, an offspring born of another is no offspring; do not lead us away from the path of one who is wise.** ॥ ७ ॥

**Word-for-word analysis:**
परि॑ऽसद्यं (To be avoided/surrounded) । हि (for) । अ॒र॒णस्य॑ (of a stranger/other) । रे॒क्णः॑ (wealth/inheritance) । नित्य॑स्य (of the eternal/own) । रा॒यः (of wealth) । पत॑यः (masters) । स्याम (may we be) ।
न (not) । शेषः॑ (offspring/remainder) । अ॒ग्ने॒ (O Agni) । अ॒न्यऽजा॑तं (born of another) । अ॒स्ति (is) । अ॒चे॒तानस्य (of the ignorant/unwise) । मा (not) । प॒थः (from the path) । वि (away) । दुक्षः (lead/milk) ॥ ७ ॥

---

## Commentary (Sayana)

The **wealth** <note>original: "rekṇaḥ"</note> of a **stranger** <note>original: "araṇasya"</note>—meaning someone else—is **to be avoided** <note>original: "pariṣadyaṃ"</note> or is merely something that surrounds us but isn't truly ours. Therefore, **may we be the masters** <note>original: "patayaḥ syāma"</note> of **eternal** <note>original: "nityasya"</note> **wealth** <note>original: "rāyaḥ"</note>—that which does not have to be given back. Alternatively, the wealth of a stranger is something to be shunned...

<vocab>
<term>Agni</term> : The Vedic deity of fire, seen as the priest of the gods and the mediator between heaven and earth.
<term>Kratu</term> : A complex term meaning intelligence, will, or the sacrificial power/wisdom that guides ritual action.
<term>Amrita</term> : Literally "not-death"; refers to the drink of the gods, immortality, or in a ritual context, the sustaining waters or sacrificial offerings.
<term>Oshadhi</term> : Herbs or plants, frequently described in the Vedas as the "womb" where Agni (as heat or life force) resides.
<term>Sahasavan</term> : "Possessing power"; a frequent title for Agni, referring to his birth from the "force" or "strength" of rubbing fire-sticks together.
<term>Avira</term> : One who lacks "Viras" (heroes/sons); in Vedic society, having sons was essential for continuing the lineage and the ritual fire.
<term>Reknas</term> : Property, inheritance, or wealth, often specifically referring to what is handed down through a family line.
<term>Nitya</term> : Eternal, perpetual, or one's own; here used to distinguish indigenous/family wealth from that of a stranger.
</vocab>

<summary>This page concludes Sukta 4 of Mandala 7, where the sage prays to Agni for legitimate offspring and independent wealth. Sayana's commentary clarifies that Agni is the source of both immortality for the gods and material prosperity for humans, emphasizing the avoidance of relying on "strangers" for lineage or riches.</summary>
